Lauren — digging into the numbers. I ran a quick sensitivity on their projection and downside risk:

- Baseline projection (per their sheet): ~1.2M tokens month 2; 1.5M month 3.
- Upside spike scenario (3x): month 2 = 3.6M, month 3 = 4.5M.

If we do Option 1 (15k starter + 25% makeup capped at 40k): estimated expected credit exposure = $22k (95th percentile scenario), reasonably bounded.
If we do Option 2 (25k starter + 50% makeup capped at 60k): expected exposure = $41k (95th percentile), but with stronger onboarding and a 60% prepayment this nets better cash flow and reduces churn risk.

My recommendation: Approve Option 2 but with a clean cap of $50k (start + makeup combined) and require finance lock the 60% prepayment into the SOW. Also add a clause: makeup credit only applies if usage is verified against our billing logs and prompt set unchanged.

I've attached a one-pager financial-impact brief. If we want to be conservative, we can move the cap to $40k and only give 40% makeup.
